steps.say: Three glands fail in a fixed order here, and the exam always opens with the earliest. Hyperparathyroidism appears first and involves everyone by fifty, so calcium screening starts in childhood. Prolactinoma leads the pituitary half while tiny duodenal gastrinomas lead the gut half. RET driven MEN2 differs with medullary thyroid and adrenal tumours instead.
steps.tx: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (**MEN1**, menin protein) is autosomal dominant loss of the MEN1 tumour suppressor on 11q13, producing the 3 Ps: **parathyroid** multigland hyperplasia with primary hyperparathyroidism (excess parathyroid hormone) in nearly 100 percent by age 50 as the earliest feature, **pituitary** adenomas led by prolactinoma (prolactin tumour), and **pancreaticoduodenal** neuroendocrine tumours led by duodenal gastrinoma (gastrin tumour). Calcium screening starts at age 8 and pituitary screening at age 5. MEN2 runs on RET with medullary thyroid cancer, while MEN4 (CDKN1B) mimics MEN1 rarely.

vis.alt: Pituitary, parathyroid, pancreatic and duodenal lesions in MEN1.
vis.caption: Three gland tumours of MEN1 across pituitary, parathyroid and gut. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Smooth versus jagged borders separate the two great spot syndromes at a glance. California smooth indicates NF1 while Maine jagged indicates GNAS mosaic disease. Freckles in hidden skin plus iris nodules confirm NF1 clinically. Optic gliomas and nerve sheath cancers then set the surveillance list.
steps.tx: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (**NF1**, von Recklinghausen disease) is autosomal dominant loss of neurofibromin on 17q11.2, a RAS GTPase activating protein (a RAS off switch) whose failure unleashes RAS signalling (growth signalling). Hallmarks are multiple cutaneous and plexiform neurofibromas (nerve sheath tumours), six or more **Coast of California** cafe au lait macules (brown birthmarks), axillary freckling (Crowe sign), iris Lisch nodules (pigmented hamartomas), optic pathway gliomas, malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumours and phaeochromocytoma. Jagged Coast of Maine spots with fibrous dysplasia instead mean GNAS mosaicism, while bilateral vestibular schwannomas mean NF2.

vis.alt: Cafe au lait macule border types with freckling.
vis.caption: Spot borders and freckling separating NF1 from mosaic disease. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Deafness on both sides in a young adult suggests NF2 before any scan. Vestibular tumours grow on both balance nerves together, which no sporadic case copies. Meningiomas and cataracts follow across decades. Family history plus unilateral deafness still requires MRI of both ear canals.
steps.tx: Neurofibromatosis type 2 (**NF2**) is autosomal dominant loss of merlin (schwannomin) on 22q12, producing bilateral vestibular schwannomas (balance nerve tumours) in 95 to 100 percent with sensorineural hearing loss (nerve deafness), meningiomas in about 50 percent, spinal ependymomas (cord lining tumours) and juvenile posterior subcapsular cataracts (lens clouding), remembered as **MISME** (multiple inherited schwannomas, meningiomas and ependymomas). One sided deafness with a family story triggers MRI of the internal auditory meati (ear canals).

vis.alt: Cerebellopontine angle vestibular schwannoma with Verocay bodies.
vis.caption: Vestibular schwannoma with Verocay body histology in NF2. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Kidney screening in VHL starts at fifteen, well before tumours threaten the nephron sparing window. Eye and catecholamine checks start even earlier in childhood. Lynch puts bowel first and womb second, which guides the surveillance organs. Gene panels now test both syndromes together when family trees overlap.
steps.tx: Von Hippel Lindau disease (**VHL**, 3p25) pairs retinal and cerebellar haemangioblastomas with clear cell renal cancer, phaeochromocytoma and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, starting abdominal **MRI surveillance** (magnetic imaging) at age 15 every 1 to 2 years toward the 3 cm nephron sparing surgery threshold. **Lynch syndrome** (mismatch repair loss in MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2 or EPCAM) ranks colorectal cancer first at 50 to 80 percent lifetime risk and endometrial cancer second overall but first extracolonic at 40 to 60 percent, followed by ovary, stomach, bowel, urothelial, brain and skin tumours.

vis.alt: Proximal colon, endometrial and ovarian cancers with repair defect.
vis.caption: Lynch spectrum across bowel and gynaecologic organs. Credit: StewardMD.
